sections.title: Classwork — Comparing Vertical and Horizontal Translations and Dilations

questions.prompt: Activity 2.1 — Translate the graph of f(x) = x LEFT 3 units. Call the new graph t(x). Plot the image of each labeled point S1–S5, in order (S1 → P1, S2 → P2, …).
hints: Left 3 means subtract 3 from every x-coordinate.
The y-coordinates do not change for a horizontal translation.

steps.title: Move every point
steps.instruction: To translate a graph, move every point the same distance in the same direction. Left/right changes only the x-coordinate; up/down changes only the y-coordinate.

steps.title: Worked example
steps.instruction: Translating f(x) = x right 5 units sends (−2, −2) to (3, −2): add 5 to the input, keep the output.

questions.prompt: Translate the graph of f(x) = x UP 3 units. Call the new graph w(x). Plot the image of each labeled point S1–S5, in order.
hints: Up 3 means add 3 to every y-coordinate.
The x-coordinates do not change for a vertical translation.

questions.prompt: Compare your two graphs: t(x) is f(x) = x translated left 3, and w(x) is f(x) = x translated up 3.

responses.label: Moving a graph left or right changes which values of the corresponding points?

What do you notice about the graphs of t(x) and w(x)?
options: They intersect at exactly one point.

hints: Look at your two tables of points: which coordinate changed?
A move left or right is written inside the parentheses, with x. Which sign moves the graph left?
Simplify t(x) and w(x) with f(x) = x, then compare the two results.

steps.title: Function notation
steps.instruction: y = f(x − c) moves the graph horizontally: right when c > 0, left when c < 0. So f(x + 3) = f(x − (−3)) moves left 3.

steps.title: Outside vs. inside
steps.instruction: y = f(x) + d moves the graph vertically: up when d > 0, down when d < 0.

steps.title: Vertical dilation
steps.instruction: y = a·f(x) multiplies every output by a. |a| > 1 stretches the graph vertically; 0 < |a| < 1 compresses it; a < 0 also reflects it across the x-axis.

questions.prompt: Change the INPUT values of f(x) = x by a factor of 1/2 to create b(x). Plot the image of each labeled point, in order. (The grid snaps to halves.)
hints: Multiply each x-coordinate by 1/2.
Keep each y-coordinate.

steps.title: Horizontal dilation
steps.instruction: y = f(bx) multiplies every input by 1/b. |b| > 1 compresses the graph horizontally by a factor of 1/|b|; 0 < |b| < 1 stretches it; b < 0 also reflects it across the y-axis.

questions.prompt: Essential Question: what effect do horizontal transformations have on linear functions, and how do they compare to vertical transformations?

responses.label: A horizontal change, f(x − c) or f(bx), acts on the …

optionRationales.input values (x-coordinates): A change inside the parentheses happens to x before f acts, so it moves or scales the x-coordinates.
optionRationales.output values (y-coordinates): Changes to outputs sit outside f, like f(x) + c or a·f(x); here the change is written inside the parentheses.
optionRationales.slope only: Slope is a feature of the result, not what the change acts on; f(x − c) can leave the slope the same.
optionRationales.y-intercept only: The y-intercept is a feature of the result, not what the change acts on; f(bx) can leave it the same.

responses.label: For f(x) = x, which function has the same graph as 4f(x)?

optionRationales.f(4x): For f(x) = x, f(4x) = 4x, which is exactly 4f(x) = 4x.
optionRationales.f((1/4)x): This uses the reciprocal, as a horizontal stretch would: f((1/4)x) = (1/4)x, a smaller slope than 4f(x).
optionRationales.f(x + 4): This adds 4 instead of multiplying by 4: f(x + 4) = x + 4.
optionRationales.f(x) + 4: This adds 4 to the output instead of multiplying it by 4: f(x) + 4 = x + 4.

responses.label: For f(x) = x, moving the graph left n units gives the same graph as …

optionRationales.moving it up n units: Left n units is f(x + n) = x + n, which is also f(x) + n: y = x looks the same moved up n.
optionRationales.moving it down n units: This pairs left with down by direction; for y = x, compare f(x + n) with f(x) − n and they differ.
optionRationales.moving it right n units: Right n units is f(x − n), the opposite horizontal move, so it gives a different graph.
optionRationales.stretching it vertically by n: A stretch changes the slope of y = x, but moving the line left keeps its slope at 1.
